belief: No one will care for me when I need them.
origins: This belief often starts in homes where needs were ignored, dismissed, or punished, or where a child had to care for a parent instead of being cared for. Times of illness, crisis, or grief when no one showed up can deepen it. People who hold this belief often become fiercely self-reliant, never ask for help, and then feel confirmed when no one offers.
teaches: God invites us to cast all our anxiety on Him, because He cares for us. Jesus pointed to the birds of the air and reminded us that our Father feeds them, and we are worth much more. The Lord is near to all who call on Him. Scripture also calls believers to carry one another’s burdens; caring for each other is how God designed His family to work. People may have failed you, but God cares, and He often sends His care through people when we let them in.
self_statements: If I fall apart, no one will be there.
I have to take care of myself because no one else will.
People only show up when they need something.
My needs are a burden to others.
errors: Deciding that because some people didn’t care, no one will.
Predicting that no one will help before I ask.
Overlooking times when people did help.
Assuming others see my needs as a burden.
questions: When were my needs ignored, and by whom?
When has someone cared for me, even a little?
Do I let people know when I need help?
Am I so self-reliant that no one gets the chance to care?
What does God say about His care for me?
Who is one person I could ask for help?
truth: There were times when no one cared for me as I needed. But God cares for me, and He often sends His care through people. I can let my needs be known, ask for help, and give others the chance to show up.
hw_truths: I can cast my burdens on the Lord.
My Father knows what I need.
Asking for help is not weakness.
God’s family is meant to carry burdens together.
The Lord is near when I call.
log: Each day, write one way someone cared for you, or one time you asked for help and what happened.
actions: Write the names of people you could call in a hard moment, even if you have never asked. Add a church or helpline.
Ask one person for a small, specific favor this week. Note how they responded.
When asked “How are you?” give one honest answer instead of “Fine.”
Each morning, tell God one specific need, following 1 Peter 5:7.
prayer: Father, I have felt alone in my needs for a long time. Thank You that You care for me and that I can bring every burden to You. Help me let others in, ask for help, and receive the care You send. Amen.
